This is a general overview and status of places affected by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SARS-CoV-2 "SARS-CoV-2") (SARS-CoV-2), the virus which causes coronavirus disease 2019 ([COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19")) and is responsible for the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). The first human cases of COVID-19 were identified in [Wuhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan "Wuhan"), the capital of the province of [Hubei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubei "Hubei") in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") in December 2019. It spread to other areas of Asia, and then worldwide in early 2020.

The figures presented are based on reported cases and deaths. While in several high-income countries the ratio of total estimated cases and deaths to reported cases and deaths is low and close to 1, for some countries it may be more than 10[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_by_country_and_territory#cite_note-8) or even more than 100.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_by_country_and_territory#cite_note-9) Implementation of [COVID-19 surveillance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_surveillance "COVID-19 surveillance") methods varies widely.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_by_country_and_territory#cite_note-10)

This is a general overview and status of places affected by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SARS-CoV-2 "SARS-CoV-2") (SARS-CoV-2), the virus which causes coronavirus disease 2019 ([COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19")) and is responsible for the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). The first human cases of COVID-19 were identified in [Wuhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuhan "Wuhan"), the capital of the province of [Hubei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubei "Hubei") in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") in December 2019. It spread to other areas of Asia, and then worldwide in early 2020.

The figures presented are based on reported cases and deaths. While in several high-income countries the ratio of total estimated cases and deaths to reported cases and deaths is low and close to 1, for some countries it may be more than 10[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_by_country_and_territory#cite_note-8) or even more than 100.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_by_country_and_territory#cite_note-9) Implementation of [COVID-19 surveillance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_surveillance "COVID-19 surveillance") methods varies widely.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_by_country_and_territory#cite_note-10)

**Hungary**[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-14) is a [landlocked country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landlocked_country "Landlocked country") in [Central Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Europe "Central Europe").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Flaw-15) Spanning much of the [Carpathian Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Basin "Pannonian Basin"), it is bordered by [Slovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovakia "Slovakia") to the north, [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") to the northeast, [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania") to the east and southeast, [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") to the south, [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") and [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia "Slovenia") to the southwest, and [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria") to the west. Hungary lies within the [Danube River's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danube "Danube")[drainage basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin") and is dominated by great lowland [plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plain "Plain"). It has a population of over 9.5 million, consisting mostly of ethnic [Hungarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarians "Hungarians") (Magyars) and a [significant Romani minority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_people_in_Hungary "Romani people in Hungary"). [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_language "Hungarian language") is the [official language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Hungary "Languages of Hungary") and among the [few in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Europe "Languages of Europe") outside the [Indo-European family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-European_languages "Indo-European languages").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-16)[Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest "Budapest") is the country's capital, [largest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_and_towns_of_Hungary "List of cities and towns of Hungary"), and cultural and economic center.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-18)

Before the establishment of the Hungarian state, the territory was settled by various groups, including [Celts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celts "Celts"), [Romans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome"), [Huns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huns "Huns"), [Germanic peoples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_peoples "Germanic peoples"), [Avars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Avars "Pannonian Avars"), and [Slavs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavs "Slavs"). Statehood began in the late ninth century with the [Principality of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Hungary "Principality of Hungary"), which became a medieval [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian "Christian") kingdom under King [Stephen I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_I_of_Hungary "Stephen I of Hungary") in 1000. After it was defeated by the [Ottoman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") at the [Battle of Mohács](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Moh%C3%A1cs "Battle of Mohács") in 1526, the kingdom was split into three regions for over 150 years until its reunion under [Habsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habsburg "Habsburg") rule before the turn of the 18th century. Several uprisings against the Habsburgs precipitated the formation of the [Austro-Hungarian Monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Monarchy "Austro-Hungarian Monarchy") in the [Compromise of 1867](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Compromise_of_1867 "Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867"); Austria-Hungary remained a European [great power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_power "Great power") until [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"). Hungary's modern borders were then established by the 1920 [Treaty of Trianon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Trianon "Treaty of Trianon"), which resulted in severe losses for the country, including 71% of its historical territory and the majority of its economy and population; [a third of ethnic Hungarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_diaspora "Hungarian diaspora") were left outside the new borders.

Hungary endured turmoil in the early [interwar period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_between_the_World_Wars "Hungary between the World Wars"), culminating in the [national-conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_conservatism "National conservatism") regime of [regent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regent_of_Hungary "Regent of Hungary")[Miklós Horthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikl%C3%B3s_Horthy "Miklós Horthy"). Hungary joined the [Axis powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers") in [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), suffering significant damage and casualties.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Montgomery-19)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Thomas,_pg._11-20) After a brief [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") occupation, the [Hungarian People's Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_People's_Republic "Hungarian People's Republic") was established in 1949 as a [satellite state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite_state "Satellite state") inside the [Warsaw Pact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact "Warsaw Pact"). Subsequent political repression and economic stagnation led to the unsuccessful [Hungarian Revolution of 1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Revolution_of_1956 "Hungarian Revolution of 1956"), though [communist rule softened](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goulash_Communism "Goulash Communism") in the following decades. During the [Revolutions of 1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989 "Revolutions of 1989"), Hungary peacefully transitioned into a [democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_republic "Democratic republic")[parliamentary republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_republic "Parliamentary republic").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-21) It joined the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") (EU) in 2004 and the [Schengen Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area "Schengen Area") in 2007. [Under the leadership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_premiership_of_Viktor_Orb%C3%A1n "Second premiership of Viktor Orbán") of [Viktor Orbán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Orb%C3%A1n "Viktor Orbán") and [Fidesz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidesz "Fidesz") from 2010 to 2026, the country experienced [democratic backsliding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_backsliding "Democratic backsliding").

"List of universities and colleges in Hungary").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-auto-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-europa-23) It has a long history ## Etymology

Main article: [Name of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_of_Hungary "Name of Hungary")

The "H" in the name of Hungary is most likely derived from historical associations with the [Huns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huns "Huns"), who had settled Hungary prior to the [Avars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Avars "Pannonian Avars").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-30) The rest of the word comes from the Latinised form of [Byzantine Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_Greek "Medieval Greek")_Oungroi_ (Οὔγγροι). The Greek name might be borrowed from [Old Slavonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Church_Slavonic "Old Church Slavonic")_ągrinŭ_, in turn borrowed from [Oghur-Turkic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oghuric_languages "Oghuric languages")_[Onogur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onogurs "Onogurs")_ ('ten [tribes of the] Ogurs').[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-31)_Onogur_ was the collective name for the tribes who later joined the [Bulgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgars "Bulgars") tribal confederacy that ruled the eastern parts of Hungary after the Avars.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kir%C3%A1ly-32)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-33)[Peter B. Golden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Benjamin_Golden "Peter Benjamin Golden") also considers the suggestion of Árpád Berta that the name derives from [Khazar Turkic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khazar_language "Khazar language")_ongar_ (oŋ "right", oŋar- "to make something better, to put (it) right", oŋgar- "to make something better, to put (it) right", oŋaru "towards the right") "right wing". This points to the idea that the Magyar Union before the Conquest formed the "right wing" (western wing) of the [Khazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khazars "Khazars") military forces.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-34)

The Hungarian [endonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endonym_and_exonym "Endonym and exonym") is _Magyarország_, composed of _magyar_ ('Hungarian') and _ország_ ('country'). The name "Magyar", which refers to the people of the country, more accurately reflects the name of the country in some other languages such as [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_language "Turkish language"), [Persian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_language "Persian language") and other languages as _Magyaristan_ or _Land of Magyars_ or similar. The word _magyar_ is taken from the name of the leading tribe of the seven major semi-nomadic Hungarian tribes.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-35)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-37)

## History

Main article: [History of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Hungary "History of Hungary")

### Before 895

Main articles: [Hungarian prehistory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_prehistory "Hungarian prehistory") and [Hungarian mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_mythology "Hungarian mythology")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Pannonia_t%C3%A9rk%C3%A9p_2._sz%C3%A1zad.jpg/250px-Pannonia_t%C3%A9rk%C3%A9p_2._sz%C3%A1zad.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pannonia_t%C3%A9rk%C3%A9p_2._sz%C3%A1zad.jpg)

Roman provinces and barbarian peoples in and near the [Carpathian Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Basin "Pannonian Basin") in the 2nd century AD

The [Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire "Roman Empire") conquered the territory between the [Alps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alps "Alps") and the area west of the [Danube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danube "Danube") River from 16 to 15 BC, the Danube being the frontier of the empire.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kershaw-38) In 14 BC, [Pannonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonia "Pannonia"), the western part of the [Carpathian Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Basin "Pannonian Basin"), which includes the west of today's Hungary, was recognised by emperor [Augustus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustus "Augustus") in the _[Res Gestae Divi Augusti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Res\_Gestae\_Divi\_Augusti "Res Gestae Divi Augusti")_ as part of the Roman Empire.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kershaw-38) The area south-east of Pannonia was organised as the Roman province [Moesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moesia "Moesia") in 6 BC.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kershaw-38) An area east of the river [Tisza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisza "Tisza") became the Roman province of [Dacia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacia "Dacia") in 106 AD, which included today's east Hungary. It remained under Roman rule until 271.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Scarre-39)

From 235, the Roman Empire went through troubled times, caused by revolts, rivalry and rapid succession of emperors. The Western Roman Empire collapsed in the 5th century under the stress of the migration of [Germanic tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_peoples "Germanic peoples") and [Carpian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpi_people "Carpi people") pressure.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Scarre-39) This period brought many invaders into Central Europe, beginning with the [Hunnic Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huns "Huns") (c.370–469). The most powerful ruler of the Hunnic Empire was [Attila the Hun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attila "Attila") (434–453), who later became a central figure in Hungarian mythology.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kelly-40) After the disintegration of the Hunnic Empire, the [Gepids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gepids "Gepids"), an Eastern Germanic tribe, who had been vassalised by the Huns, established their own kingdom in the Carpathian Basin.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Bona_The_Gepids_during_and_after_the_Hun_Period-41) Other groups which reached the Carpathian Basin during the Migration Period were the [Goths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goths "Goths"), [Vandals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vandals "Vandals"), [Lombards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lombards "Lombards"), and [Slavs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Slavs "Early Slavs").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Scarre-39)

In the 560s, the [Avars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Avars "Pannonian Avars") founded the Avar Khaganate, a state that maintained supremacy in the region for more than two centuries. The [Franks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franks "Franks") under [Charlemagne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlemagne "Charlemagne") defeated the Avars in a series of campaigns during the 790s.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Gubcsi-42) Between 804 and 829, the [First Bulgarian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Bulgarian_Empire "First Bulgarian Empire") conquered the lands east of the Danube and took over the rule of the local Slavic tribes and remnants of the Avars.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Skutsch-43) By the mid-9th century, the [Balaton Principality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavs_in_Lower_Pannonia#Principality "Slavs in Lower Pannonia"), also known as Lower Pannonia, was established west of the Danube as part of the Frankish [March of Pannonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_of_Pannonia "March of Pannonia").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Luthar-44)

### Middle Ages (895–1526)

Main articles: [Principality of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Hungary "Principality of Hungary") and [Kingdom of Hungary in the Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary_in_the_Middle_Ages "Kingdom of Hungary in the Middle Ages")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Kalandozasok.jpg/250px-Kalandozasok.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kalandozasok.jpg)

[Hungarian raids in the 9–10th centuries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_invasions_of_Europe "Hungarian invasions of Europe"): Between 899 and 970, the researchers count 47 (38 to West and 9 to East)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Szabados_Augsburg_2005-45) raids in different parts of Europe. From these campaigns only 8 were unsuccessful and the others ended with success.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-FOOTNOTENagy2007168-46)

The foundation of the [Hungarian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Hungary "Principality of Hungary") is connected to the [Hungarian conquerors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_conquest_of_the_Carpathian_Basin "Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin"), who arrived from the [Pontic-Caspian steppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontic%E2%80%93Caspian_steppe "Pontic–Caspian steppe") as a confederation of [seven tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_chieftains_of_the_Magyars "Seven chieftains of the Magyars").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-c194-47) The [Hungarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarians "Hungarians") arrived in the [Carpathian Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Basin "Pannonian Basin") as a branch of a strong centralised steppe-empire under the leadership of Grand Prince [Álmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lmos "Álmos") and his son [Árpád](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81rp%C3%A1d "Árpád"): founders of the [Árpád dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81rp%C3%A1d_dynasty "Árpád dynasty"), the Hungarian ruling dynasty and the Hungarian state. The Árpád dynasty claimed to be a direct descendant of [Attila the Hun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attila "Attila").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-:02-48)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-49)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-50) The Hungarians took possession of the area in a pre-planned manner, with a long move-in between 862 and 895.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-:2822-51) The rising Hungary conducted successful [fierce campaigns and raids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_invasions_of_Europe "Hungarian invasions of Europe"), from [Constantinople](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantinople "Constantinople") to as far as today's Spain.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Stephen_Wyley-52) The Hungarians defeated three major East Frankish imperial armies between 907 and 910.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-53) A defeat at the [Battle of Lechfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lechfeld "Battle of Lechfeld") in 955 signalled a provisory end to most campaigns on foreign territories, at least towards the west.

#### Age of Árpádian kings

Main articles: [Kingdom of Hungary (1000–1301)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary_(1000%E2%80%931301) "Kingdom of Hungary (1000–1301)") and [Árpád dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81rp%C3%A1d_dynasty "Árpád dynasty")

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/A_Szent_Korona_el%C3%B6lr%C5%91l_2.jpg/250px-A_Szent_Korona_el%C3%B6lr%C5%91l_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:A_Szent_Korona_el%C3%B6lr%C5%91l_2.jpg)

The [Holy Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Crown_of_Hungary "Holy Crown of Hungary") (_Szent Korona_), one of the key symbols of Hungary. It was gifted to [Saint Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_I_of_Hungary "Stephen I of Hungary"), the first [King of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Hungary "King of Hungary"), who converted the nation to Christianity.

In 972, the ruling prince ([Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_language "Hungarian language"): _fejedelem_) [Géza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%A9za,_Grand_Prince_of_the_Hungarians "Géza, Grand Prince of the Hungarians") of the [Árpád dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81rp%C3%A1d_dynasty "Árpád dynasty") officially started to integrate Hungary into Christian Western Europe.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-54) His son [Saint Stephen I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_I_of_Hungary "Stephen I of Hungary") became the first [King of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Hungary "King of Hungary") after defeating his [pagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paganism "Paganism") uncle [Koppány](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kopp%C3%A1ny "Koppány"). Under Stephen, Hungary was recognised as a Catholic [Apostolic Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Majesty "Apostolic Majesty").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-55) Applying to [Pope Sylvester II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Sylvester_II "Pope Sylvester II"), Stephen received the insignia of royalty (including probably a part of the [Holy Crown of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Crown_of_Hungary "Holy Crown of Hungary")) from the papacy.

By 1006, Stephen consolidated his power and started sweeping reforms to convert Hungary into a Western-style [feudal state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feudalism "Feudalism"). The country switched to using Latin for administration purposes, and until as late as 1844, Latin remained the official language of administration. King [Saint Ladislaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladislaus_I_of_Hungary "Ladislaus I of Hungary") completed the work of King [Saint Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_I_of_Hungary "Stephen I of Hungary"), consolidating the Hungarian state's power and strengthening [Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"). His charismatic personality, strategic leadership, and military talents resulted in the termination of internal power struggles and foreign military threats.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Saint_Ladislaus_DNA-56) The wife of the Croatian king [Demetrius Zvonimir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demetrius_Zvonimir_of_Croatia "Demetrius Zvonimir of Croatia") was Ladislaus's sister.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-57) At [Helen's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_of_Hungary,_Queen_of_Croatia "Helen of Hungary, Queen of Croatia") request, Ladislaus intervened in the conflict and invaded Croatia in 1091.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFine1991282,_284-58) The [Kingdom of Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Croatia_(925%E2%80%931102) "Kingdom of Croatia (925–1102)") entered a [personal union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_in_personal_union_with_Hungary "Croatia in personal union with Hungary") with the [Kingdom of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary_(1000%E2%80%931301) "Kingdom of Hungary (1000–1301)") in 1102 with the coronation of King [Coloman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coloman,_King_of_Hungary "Coloman, King of Hungary") as "King of Croatia and Dalmatia" in 1102 in [Biograd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biograd_na_Moru "Biograd na Moru").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-HR-HU-Heka-59)

[![Image 18: 1097, Europe, map](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/12/Europe_mediterranean_1097.jpg/250px-Europe_mediterranean_1097.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Europe_mediterranean_1097.jpg)

Europe in 1097

One of the most powerful and wealthiest kings of the Árpád dynasty was [Béla III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9la_III_of_Hungary "Béla III of Hungary"),[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-60) who disposed of the equivalent of 23 tonnes of silver per year, according to a contemporary [income register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_register_of_B%C3%A9la_III_of_Hungary "Income register of Béla III of Hungary"). This exceeded the income of the French king (estimated at 17 tonnes) and was double the receipts of the English Crown.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-61)[Andrew II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_II_of_Hungary "Andrew II of Hungary") issued the _[Diploma Andreanum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diploma\_Andreanum "Diploma Andreanum")_ which secured the special privileges of the [Transylvanian Saxons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transylvanian_Saxons "Transylvanian Saxons") and is considered the first [autonomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_administrative_division "Autonomous administrative division") law in the world.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-62) He led the [Fifth Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Crusade "Fifth Crusade") to the [Holy Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Land "Holy Land") in 1217, setting up the largest royal army in the history of Crusades. His [Golden Bull of 1222](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Bull_of_1222 "Golden Bull of 1222") was the first constitution in [Continental Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Europe "Continental Europe"). The lesser nobles also began to present Andrew with grievances, a practice that evolved into the institution of the parliament (_parlamentum publicum_).

In 1241–1242, the kingdom received a major blow with the [Mongol (Tatar) invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongolian_invasion_of_Hungary "Mongolian invasion of Hungary"). Up to half of Hungary's population of 2 million were victims of the invasion.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-63) King [Béla IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9la_IV_of_Hungary "Béla IV of Hungary") let [Cumans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumans "Cumans") and [Jassic people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jasz_people "Jasz people"), who were fleeing the Mongols, into the country.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-64) Over the centuries, they were fully assimilated.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-65) After the Mongols retreated, King Béla ordered the construction of hundreds of stone castles and fortifications, to defend against a possible second Mongol invasion. The [Mongols returned to Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Mongol_invasion_of_Hungary "Second Mongol invasion of Hungary") in 1285, but the newly built stone-castle systems and new tactics (using a higher proportion of heavily armed knights) stopped them. The invading Mongol force was defeated[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-66) near Pest by the royal army of King [Ladislaus IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladislaus_IV_of_Hungary "Ladislaus IV of Hungary"). As with later invasions, it was repelled handily, the Mongols losing much of their invading force.

#### Age of elected kings

Main articles: [Kingdom of Hungary (1301–1526)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary_(1301%E2%80%931526) "Kingdom of Hungary (1301–1526)") and [Ottoman–Hungarian Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Hungarian_Wars "Ottoman–Hungarian Wars")

The [Kingdom of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary "Kingdom of Hungary") reached one of its greatest extents during the Árpádian kings, yet royal power was weakened at the end of their rule in 1301. After a destructive period of [interregnum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interregnum "Interregnum") (1301–1308), the first [Angevin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capetian_House_of_Anjou "Capetian House of Anjou") king, [Charles I of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_I_of_Hungary "Charles I of Hungary") – a bilineal descendant of the [Árpád dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81rp%C3%A1d_dynasty "Árpád dynasty") – successfully restored royal power and defeated oligarch rivals, the so-called "little kings". The second Angevin Hungarian king, [Louis the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_I_of_Hungary "Louis I of Hungary") (1342–1382), led many successful military campaigns from Lithuania to southern Italy ([Kingdom of Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Naples "Kingdom of Naples")) and was also [King of Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Polish_monarchs "List of Polish monarchs") from 1370. After King Louis died without a male heir, the country was stabilised only when [Sigismund of Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigismund,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor") (1387–1437) succeeded to the throne, who in 1433 also became [Holy Roman Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Roman_Emperor "Holy Roman Emperor"). The first Hungarian [Bible translation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible_translations "Bible translations") was completed in 1439. For half a year in 1437, there was an antifeudal and anticlerical [peasant revolt in Transylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transylvanian_peasant_revolt "Transylvanian peasant revolt") which was strongly influenced by [Hussite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hussite "Hussite") ideas. From a small noble family in Transylvania, [John Hunyadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hunyadi "John Hunyadi") grew to become one of the country's most powerful lords, thanks to his capabilities as a mercenary commander. He was elected governor, then regent. He was a successful crusader against the [Ottoman Turks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Turks "Ottoman Turks"), one of his greatest victories being the [siege of Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Belgrade_(1456) "Siege of Belgrade (1456)") in 1456.

[![Image 19: Portrait, Matthias Corvinus, King of Hungary, Hunyadi, relief](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Portrait_of_Matthias_Corvinus%2C_King_of_Hungary.jpg/250px-Portrait_of_Matthias_Corvinus%2C_King_of_Hungary.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Portrait_of_Matthias_Corvinus,_King_of_Hungary.jpg)

Renaissance portrait of [Matthias Corvinus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthias_Corvinus "Matthias Corvinus"), King of Hungary and Croatia (1458–1490), King of Bohemia (1469–1490) and Archduke of Austria (1487–1490)

The last strong king of medieval Hungary was the [Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance "Renaissance") king [Matthias Corvinus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthias_Corvinus "Matthias Corvinus") (1458–1490), son of John Hunyadi. His election was the first time that a member of the nobility mounted the Hungarian royal throne without a dynastic background. He was a successful military leader and an enlightened patron of the arts and learning.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-britannica1-67) His library, the [Bibliotheca Corviniana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bibliotheca_Corviniana "Bibliotheca Corviniana"), was Europe's greatest collection of historical chronicles, philosophic and scientific works in the 15th century, and second only in size to the [Vatican Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Library "Vatican Library"). Items from the Bibliotheca Corviniana were inscribed on [UNESCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")'s [Memory of the World Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_of_the_World_Programme "Memory of the World Programme") in 2005.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-68) The serfs and common people considered him a just ruler because he protected them from excessive demands and other abuses by the magnates.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-69) Under his rule, in 1479, the Hungarian army destroyed the Ottoman and Wallachian troops at the [Battle of Breadfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Breadfield "Battle of Breadfield"). Abroad, he defeated the Polish and German imperial armies of Frederick at Breslau ([Wrocław](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wroc%C5%82aw "Wrocław")). Matthias' mercenary standing army, the [Black Army of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Army_of_Hungary "Black Army of Hungary"), was an unusually large army for its time, and it conquered [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna") as well as parts of Austria and [Bohemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemia "Bohemia").

King Matthias died without lawful sons, and the Hungarian magnates procured the accession of the Pole [Vladislaus II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladislaus_II_of_Hungary "Vladislaus II of Hungary") (1490–1516), supposedly because of his weak influence on Hungarian aristocracy.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-britannica1-67) Hungary's international role declined, its political stability was shaken, and social progress was deadlocked.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-70) In 1514, the weakened old King Vladislaus II faced a major peasant rebellion led by [György Dózsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gy%C3%B6rgy_D%C3%B3zsa "György Dózsa"), which was ruthlessly crushed by the [nobles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_nobility "Hungarian nobility"), led by [John Zápolya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Z%C3%A1polya "John Zápolya"). The resulting degradation of order paved the way for Ottoman preeminence. In 1521, the strongest Hungarian fortress in the South, Nándorfehérvár (today's [Belgrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade"), Serbia), [fell to the Turks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Belgrade_(1521) "Siege of Belgrade (1521)"). The early appearance of Protestantism further worsened internal relations in the country.

### Ottoman wars (1526–1699)

Main articles: [Kingdom of Hungary (1526–1867)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary_(1526%E2%80%931867) "Kingdom of Hungary (1526–1867)"), [Ottoman Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Hungary "Ottoman Hungary"), and [Eastern Hungarian Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Hungarian_Kingdom "Eastern Hungarian Kingdom")

See also: [Principality of Transylvania (1570–1711)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Transylvania_(1570%E2%80%931711) "Principality of Transylvania (1570–1711)") and [Ottoman–Habsburg wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Habsburg_wars "Ottoman–Habsburg wars")

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Sz%C3%A9kely%2C_Bertalan_-_The_Women_of_Eger_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg/250px-Sz%C3%A9kely%2C_Bertalan_-_The_Women_of_Eger_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sz%C3%A9kely,_Bertalan_-_The_Women_of_Eger_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg)

"The Women of Eger", oil painting from 1867 commemorating the [siege of Eger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Eger_(1552) "Siege of Eger (1552)"), a major victory against the Ottomans

After some [150 years of wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_wars_in_Europe "Ottoman wars in Europe") with the Hungarians and other states, the Ottomans gained a decisive victory over the Hungarian army at the [Battle of Mohács](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Moh%C3%A1cs "Battle of Mohács") in 1526, where King [Louis II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_II_of_Hungary "Louis II of Hungary") died while fleeing. Amid political chaos, the divided Hungarian nobility elected two kings simultaneously, [John Zápolya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Z%C3%A1polya "John Zápolya") and [Ferdinand I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_I,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Ferdinand I, Holy Roman Emperor") of the [Habsburg dynasty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Habsburg "House of Habsburg"). With the conquest of [Buda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buda "Buda") by the Turks in 1541, Hungary was divided into three parts and remained so until the end of the 17th century. The north-western part, termed as [Royal Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Hungary "Royal Hungary"), was annexed by the Habsburgs, who ruled as kings of Hungary. The eastern part of the kingdom became independent as the [Principality of Transylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Transylvania_(1570%E2%80%931711) "Principality of Transylvania (1570–1711)"), under Ottoman (and later Habsburg) [suzerainty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzerainty "Suzerainty"). The remaining central area, including the capital Buda, was known as the Pashalik of Buda.

In 1686, the [Holy League's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_League_(1684) "Holy League (1684)") army, containing over 74,000 men from various nations, [reconquered Buda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Buda_(1686) "Siege of Buda (1686)") from the Turks. After some more crushing [defeats of the Ottomans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Turkish_War_(1716%E2%80%931718) "Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718)") in the next few years, the entire Kingdom of Hungary was removed from Ottoman rule by 1718. The last raid into Hungary by the Ottoman vassals [Tatars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Khanate "Crimean Khanate") from [Crimea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimea "Crimea") took place in 1717.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-71) The constrained Habsburg Counter-Reformation efforts in the 17th century reconverted the majority of the kingdom to Catholicism. The ethnic composition of Hungary was fundamentally changed as a consequence of the prolonged warfare with the Turks. A large part of the country became devastated, population growth was stunted, and many smaller settlements perished.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-72) The Austrian-Habsburg government settled large groups of [Serbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbs "Serbs") and other Slavs in the depopulated south, and settled [Germans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germans_of_Hungary "Germans of Hungary") (called [Danube Swabians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danube_Swabians "Danube Swabians")) in various areas, but Hungarians were not allowed to settle or re-settle in the south of the Carpathian Basin.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-73)

### From the 18th century to World War I (1699–1918)

Main articles: [Rákóczi's War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A1k%C3%B3czi's_War_of_Independence "Rákóczi's War of Independence"), [Hungarian Reform Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Reform_Era "Hungarian Reform Era"), [Hungarian Revolution of 1848](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Revolution_of_1848 "Hungarian Revolution of 1848"), [Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lands_of_the_Crown_of_Saint_Stephen "Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen"), and [Hungary in World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_in_World_War_I "Hungary in World War I")

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/M%C3%A1nyoki%2C_%C3%81dam_-_Portrait_of_Prince_Ferenc_R%C3%A1k%C3%B3czi_II_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg/250px-M%C3%A1nyoki%2C_%C3%81dam_-_Portrait_of_Prince_Ferenc_R%C3%A1k%C3%B3czi_II_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:M%C3%A1nyoki,_%C3%81dam_-_Portrait_of_Prince_Ferenc_R%C3%A1k%C3%B3czi_II_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg)

[Francis II Rákóczi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_II_R%C3%A1k%C3%B3czi "Francis II Rákóczi"), leader of the war of independence against Habsburg rule (1703–1711)

Between 1703 and 1711, there was a large-scale [war of independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R%C3%A1k%C3%B3czi's_War_of_Independence "Rákóczi's War of Independence") led by [Francis II Rákóczi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_II_R%C3%A1k%C3%B3czi "Francis II Rákóczi"), who after the dethronement of the Habsburgs in 1707 at the Diet of [Ónod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93nod "Ónod"), took power provisionally as the ruling prince for the wartime period, but refused the Hungarian crown and the title "king". The uprisings lasted for years. The Hungarian [Kuruc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuruc "Kuruc") army, although taking over most of the country, lost the main [battle at Trencsén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Tren%C4%8D%C3%ADn "Battle of Trenčín") (1708). Three years later, because of the growing desertion, defeatism, and low morale, the Kuruc forces surrendered.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-74)

During the [Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars") and afterward, the Hungarian Diet had not convened for decades.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-75) In the 1820s, the emperor was forced to convene the Diet, which marked the beginning of a Reform Period (1825–1848, [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_language "Hungarian language"): _reformkor_). The Hungarian Parliament was reconvened in 1825 to handle financial needs. A liberal party emerged and focused on providing for the peasantry. [Lajos Kossuth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lajos_Kossuth "Lajos Kossuth") emerged as a leader of the lower [gentry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentry "Gentry") in the Parliament. A remarkable upswing started as the nation concentrated its forces on modernisation, even though the Habsburg monarchs obstructed all important liberal laws relating to [civil and political rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_and_political_rights "Civil and political rights") and economic reforms. Many reformers (Lajos Kossuth, [Mihály Táncsics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mih%C3%A1ly_T%C3%A1ncsics "Mihály Táncsics")) were imprisoned by the authorities.

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/E._Poulton_Portrait_of_Lajos_Kossuth_1860s.jpg/250px-E._Poulton_Portrait_of_Lajos_Kossuth_1860s.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:E._Poulton_Portrait_of_Lajos_Kossuth_1860s.jpg)

[Lajos Kossuth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lajos_Kossuth "Lajos Kossuth"), Regent-President during the [Hungarian Revolution of 1848](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Revolution_of_1848 "Hungarian Revolution of 1848")

On 15 March 1848, mass demonstrations in Pest and Buda enabled Hungarian reformists to push through a list of [12 demands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12_points_of_the_Hungarian_Revolutionaries_of_1848 "12 points of the Hungarian Revolutionaries of 1848"). Under Governor and President [Lajos Kossuth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lajos_Kossuth "Lajos Kossuth") and Prime Minister [Lajos Batthyány](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lajos_Batthy%C3%A1ny "Lajos Batthyány"), the House of Habsburg was dethroned. The Habsburg ruler and his advisors skillfully manipulated the Croatian, Serbian and Romanian peasantry, led by priests and officers firmly loyal to the Habsburgs, into rebelling against the Hungarian government, though the Hungarians were supported by the vast majority of the Slovak, German and [Rusyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rusyns "Rusyns") nationalities and by all the Jews of the kingdom, as well as by a large number of Polish, Austrian and Italian volunteers.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-76) In July 1849, the Hungarian Parliament proclaimed and enacted the first laws of ethnic and [minority rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minority_rights "Minority rights") in the world.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-77) Many members of minority nationalities, like [János Damjanich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A1nos_Damjanich "János Damjanich") and [Józef Bem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%B3zef_Bem "Józef Bem"), gained the coveted highest positions within the Hungarian Army. The Hungarian forces (_[Honvédség](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal\_Hungarian\_Landwehr "Royal Hungarian Landwehr")_) defeated the Austrian armies. To counter the successes of the Hungarian revolutionary army, Habsburg Emperor [Franz Joseph I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Joseph_I_of_Austria "Franz Joseph I of Austria") asked for help from the "Gendarme of Europe", Tsar [Nicholas I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_I_of_Russia "Nicholas I of Russia"), whose Russian armies invaded Hungary. This made [Artúr Görgey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art%C3%BAr_G%C3%B6rgei "Artúr Görgei") surrender in August 1849. The leader of the Austrian army, [Julius Jacob von Haynau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Jacob_von_Haynau "Julius Jacob von Haynau"), became governor of Hungary for a few months and ordered the execution of [the 13 Martyrs of Arad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_13_Martyrs_of_Arad "The 13 Martyrs of Arad"), leaders of the Hungarian army, and Prime Minister Batthyány in October 1849. Kossuth escaped into exile. Following the war of 1848–1849, the whole country was in "passive resistance".

Because of external and internal problems, reforms seemed inevitable, and major military defeats of Austria forced the Habsburgs to negotiate the [Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Compromise_of_1867 "Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867"), by which the dual monarchy of [Austria-Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria-Hungary "Austria-Hungary") was formed. This empire had the second largest area in Europe (after the [Russian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire "Russian Empire")), and it was the third most populous (after Russia and the [German Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Empire "German Empire")). The two realms were governed separately by two parliaments from two capital cities, with a common monarch and common external and military policies. Economically, the empire was a customs union. The old Hungarian Constitution was restored, and Franz Joseph I was crowned as [King of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Hungary "King of Hungary"). The era witnessed impressive economic development. The formerly backward Hungarian economy became relatively modern and industrialised by the turn of the 20th century, although agriculture remained dominant until 1890.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-78) In 1873, the old capital Buda and [Óbuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%93buda "Óbuda") were officially united with [Pest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pest,_Hungary "Pest, Hungary"),[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-79) creating the new metropolis of Budapest.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-80)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-81) Many of the state institutions and the modern administrative system of Hungary were established during this period.

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Austria-Hungary_map.svg/250px-Austria-Hungary_map.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Austria-Hungary_map.svg)

The [Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lands_of_the_Crown_of_Saint_Stephen "Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen") consisted of the territories of the [Kingdom of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary "Kingdom of Hungary") (16) and the [Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Croatia-Slavonia "Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia") (17).

After the [assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Archduke_Franz_Ferdinand "Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand") in Sarajevo, Prime Minister [István Tisza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istv%C3%A1n_Tisza "István Tisza") and his cabinet tried to avoid the outbreak and escalation of a war in Europe, but their diplomatic efforts were unsuccessful. Austria-Hungary drafted over 4 million soldiers from the Kingdom of Hungary on the side of Germany, Bulgaria, and Turkey. The troops raised in the Kingdom of Hungary spent little time defending the actual territory of Hungary, with the exceptions of the [Brusilov offensive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brusilov_offensive "Brusilov offensive") in June 1916 and a few months later when the Romanian army made an [attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Transylvania "Battle of Transylvania") into Transylvania,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-82)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-83) both of which were repelled. The [Central Powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Powers "Central Powers") conquered Serbia, southern Romania, and the Romanian capital [Bucharest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bucharest "Bucharest"). In 1916, Franz Joseph died, and the new monarch [Charles IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_I_of_Austria "Charles I of Austria") sympathised with the pacifists. With great difficulty, the Central Powers stopped and repelled the attacks of the Russian Empire.

The [Eastern Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Front_(World_War_I) "Eastern Front (World War I)") of the Allied ([Entente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_I "Allies of World War I")) Powers completely collapsed. The Austro-Hungarian Empire then withdrew from all defeated countries. Despite great success on the Eastern Front, Germany suffered complete defeat on the [Western Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Front_(World_War_I) "Western Front (World War I)"). By 1918, the economic situation had deteriorated (strikes in factories were organised by leftist and pacifist movements) and uprisings in the army had become common. In the capital cities, the Austrian and Hungarian leftist liberal movements and their leaders supported the separatism of ethnic minorities. Austria-Hungary signed a general armistice in [Padua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padua "Padua") on 3 November 1918.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-84) In October 1918, Hungary's union with Austria was dissolved.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-85)

### Between the World Wars (1918–1941)

Main articles: [Hungary between the World Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_between_the_World_Wars "Hungary between the World Wars"), [Hungarian interwar economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_interwar_economy "Hungarian interwar economy"), and [Treaty of Trianon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Trianon "Treaty of Trianon")

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/Trianon_consequences.png/250px-Trianon_consequences.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trianon_consequences.png)

With the 1920 [Treaty of Trianon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Trianon "Treaty of Trianon"), Hungary lost 72% of its territory, its sea ports, and 3,425,000 ethnic Hungarians.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-86)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-87)

Majority Hungarian areas (according to the 1910 census) detached from Hungary

Following the First World War, Hungary underwent a period of profound political upheaval, beginning with the [Aster Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aster_Revolution "Aster Revolution") in 1918, which brought the social-democratic [Mihály Károlyi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mih%C3%A1ly_K%C3%A1rolyi "Mihály Károlyi") to power as prime minister. The [Hungarian Royal Honvéd army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Hungarian_Honv%C3%A9d "Royal Hungarian Honvéd") still had more than 1,400,000 soldiers[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-88)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-89) when Károlyi was installed. Károlyi yielded to U.S. President [Woodrow Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson "Woodrow Wilson")'s demand for [pacifism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacifism "Pacifism") by ordering the disarmament of the Hungarian army.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Dixon_1986-90)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Sharp_2008-91) Disarmament meant that Hungary was to remain without a national defence at a time of particular vulnerability. During the rule of Károlyi's pacifist cabinet, Hungary lost control over approximately 75% of its pre-war territories (325,411 square kilometres (125,642 sq mi)) without a fight and was subject to foreign occupation. The [Little Entente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Entente "Little Entente"), sensing an opportunity, invaded the country from three sides—[Romania invaded Transylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian-Romanian_War "Hungarian-Romanian War"), Czechoslovakia annexed [Upper Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Hungary "Upper Hungary") (today's Slovakia), and a joint [Serb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Serbia "Kingdom of Serbia")-[French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Army "French Army") coalition annexed [Vojvodina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vojvodina "Vojvodina") and other southern regions. In March 1919, communists led by [Béla Kun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9la_Kun "Béla Kun") ousted the Károlyi government and proclaimed the [Hungarian Soviet Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Soviet_Republic "Hungarian Soviet Republic") (_Tanácsköztársaság_), followed by a thorough [Red Terror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Terror_(Hungary) "Red Terror (Hungary)") campaign. Despite some successes on the Czechoslovak front, Kun's forces were ultimately unable to resist the Romanian invasion; by August 1919, Romanian troops occupied Budapest and ousted Kun.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-92)

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/Portraits_de_Mikl%C3%B3s_Horthy.jpg/250px-Portraits_de_Mikl%C3%B3s_Horthy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Portraits_de_Mikl%C3%B3s_Horthy.jpg)

[Miklós Horthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikl%C3%B3s_Horthy "Miklós Horthy"), Regent of the Kingdom of Hungary (1920–1944)

In November 1919, rightist forces led by former Austro-Hungarian admiral [Miklós Horthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikl%C3%B3s_Horthy "Miklós Horthy") entered Budapest; exhausted by the war and its aftermath, the populace accepted Horthy's leadership. In January 1920, parliamentary elections were held, and Horthy was proclaimed regent of the reestablished [Kingdom of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary_(1920%E2%80%931946) "Kingdom of Hungary (1920–1946)"), inaugurating the so-called "Horthy era" (_Horthy-kor_). The new government worked quickly to normalise foreign relations while turning a blind eye to a [White Terror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Terror_(Hungary) "White Terror (Hungary)") that swept through the countryside; extrajudicial killings of suspected communists and Jews lasted well into 1920.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-93)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-94)

On 4 June 1920, the [Treaty of Trianon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Trianon "Treaty of Trianon") established new borders for Hungary. The country lost 71% of its territory and 66% of its pre-war population, as well as many sources of raw materials and its sole port at [Fiume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rijeka "Rijeka").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Macartney37-95)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-NYT9Aug2003-96) An estimated 3.3 million [ethnic Hungarians were living in the ceded territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_diaspora "Hungarian diaspora"), mostly in what is now [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania"), [Slovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovakia "Slovakia") and [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia"), although modern sources for this figure range from 2 million to 5 million.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-NYT9Aug2003-96)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-97)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Sadecki2020-98) Though the revision of the treaty quickly rose to the top of the national political agenda, the Horthy government was not willing to resort to military intervention to do so.

The initial years of the Horthy regime were preoccupied with putsch attempts by [Charles IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_IV_of_Hungary "Charles IV of Hungary"), the Austro-Hungarian [pretender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretender "Pretender"); continued suppression of communists; and a migration crisis triggered by the Trianon territorial changes. The government's actions continued to drift right with the passage of [antisemitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism "Antisemitism") laws and, because of the continued isolation of the Little Entente, economic and then political gravitation towards [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy#Fascist_regime_(1922%E2%80%931943) "Kingdom of Italy") and [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany"). The [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression") further exacerbated the situation, and the popularity of fascist politicians increased, such as [Gyula Gömbös](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gyula_G%C3%B6mb%C3%B6s "Gyula Gömbös") and [Ferenc Szálasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferenc_Sz%C3%A1lasi "Ferenc Szálasi"), promising economic and social recovery. **Hungary**[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-14) is a [landlocked country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landlocked_country "Landlocked country") in [Central Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Europe "Central Europe").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Flaw-15) Spanning much of the [Carpathian Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Basin "Pannonian Basin"), it is bordered by [Slovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovakia "Slovakia") to the north, [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") to the northeast, [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania") to the east and southeast, [Serbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") to the south, [Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") and [Slovenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovenia "Slovenia") to the southwest, and [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria") to the west. Hungary lies within the [Danube River's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danube "Danube")[drainage basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin") and is dominated by great lowland [plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plain "Plain"). It has a population of over 9.5 million, consisting mostly of ethnic [Hungarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarians "Hungarians") (Magyars) and a [significant Romani minority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romani_people_in_Hungary "Romani people in Hungary"). [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_language "Hungarian language") is the [official language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Hungary "Languages of Hungary") and among the [few in Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_of_Europe "Languages of Europe") outside the [Indo-European family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-European_languages "Indo-European languages").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-16)[Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest "Budapest") is the country's capital, [largest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_and_towns_of_Hungary "List of cities and towns of Hungary"), and cultural and economic center.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-18)

Before the establishment of the Hungarian state, the territory was settled by various groups, including [Celts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celts "Celts"), [Romans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome"), [Huns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huns "Huns"), [Germanic peoples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_peoples "Germanic peoples"), [Avars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Avars "Pannonian Avars"), and [Slavs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavs "Slavs"). Statehood began in the late ninth century with the [Principality of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Hungary "Principality of Hungary"), which became a medieval [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian "Christian") kingdom under King [Stephen I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_I_of_Hungary "Stephen I of Hungary") in 1000. After it was defeated by the [Ottoman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") at the [Battle of Mohács](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Moh%C3%A1cs "Battle of Mohács") in 1526, the kingdom was split into three regions for over 150 years until its reunion under [Habsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habsburg "Habsburg") rule before the turn of the 18th century. Several uprisings against the Habsburgs precipitated the formation of the [Austro-Hungarian Monarchy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Monarchy "Austro-Hungarian Monarchy") in the [Compromise of 1867](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Compromise_of_1867 "Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867"); Austria-Hungary remained a European [great power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_power "Great power") until [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"). Hungary's modern borders were then established by the 1920 [Treaty of Trianon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Trianon "Treaty of Trianon"), which resulted in severe losses for the country, including 71% of its historical territory and the majority of its economy and population; [a third of ethnic Hungarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_diaspora "Hungarian diaspora") were left outside the new borders.

Hungary endured turmoil in the early [interwar period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary_between_the_World_Wars "Hungary between the World Wars"), culminating in the [national-conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_conservatism "National conservatism") regime of [regent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regent_of_Hungary "Regent of Hungary")[Miklós Horthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikl%C3%B3s_Horthy "Miklós Horthy"). Hungary joined the [Axis powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers") in [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), suffering significant damage and casualties.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Montgomery-19)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Thomas,_pg._11-20) After a brief [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") occupation, the [Hungarian People's Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_People's_Republic "Hungarian People's Republic") was established in 1949 as a [satellite state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite_state "Satellite state") inside the [Warsaw Pact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw_Pact "Warsaw Pact"). Subsequent political repression and economic stagnation led to the unsuccessful [Hungarian Revolution of 1956](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Revolution_of_1956 "Hungarian Revolution of 1956"), though [communist rule softened](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goulash_Communism "Goulash Communism") in the following decades. During the [Revolutions of 1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutions_of_1989 "Revolutions of 1989"), Hungary peacefully transitioned into a [democratic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_republic "Democratic republic")[parliamentary republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliamentary_republic "Parliamentary republic").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-21) It joined the [European Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Union "European Union") (EU) in 2004 and the [Schengen Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schengen_Area "Schengen Area") in 2007. [Under the leadership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_premiership_of_Viktor_Orb%C3%A1n "Second premiership of Viktor Orbán") of [Viktor Orbán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viktor_Orb%C3%A1n "Viktor Orbán") and [Fidesz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidesz "Fidesz") from 2010 to 2026, the country experienced [democratic backsliding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_backsliding "Democratic backsliding").

Hungary is a [high-income economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank_high-income_economy "World Bank high-income economy") with [universal health "List of universities and colleges in Hungary").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-auto-22)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-europa-23) It has a long history ## Etymology

Main article: [Name of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Name_of_Hungary "Name of Hungary")

The "H" in the name of Hungary is most likely derived from historical associations with the [Huns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huns "Huns"), who had settled Hungary prior to the [Avars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Avars "Pannonian Avars").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-30) The rest of the word comes from the Latinised form of [Byzantine Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medieval_Greek "Medieval Greek")_Oungroi_ (Οὔγγροι). The Greek name might be borrowed from [Old Slavonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Church_Slavonic "Old Church Slavonic")_ągrinŭ_, in turn borrowed from [Oghur-Turkic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oghuric_languages "Oghuric languages")_[Onogur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onogurs "Onogurs")_ ('ten [tribes of the] Ogurs').[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-31)_Onogur_ was the collective name for the tribes who later joined the [Bulgar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgars "Bulgars") tribal confederacy that ruled the eastern parts of Hungary after the Avars.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kir%C3%A1ly-32)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-33)[Peter B. Golden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Benjamin_Golden "Peter Benjamin Golden") also considers the suggestion of Árpád Berta that the name derives from [Khazar Turkic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khazar_language "Khazar language")_ongar_ (oŋ "right", oŋar- "to make something better, to put (it) right", oŋgar- "to make something better, to put (it) right", oŋaru "towards the right") "right wing". This points to the idea that the Magyar Union before the Conquest formed the "right wing" (western wing) of the [Khazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khazars "Khazars") military forces.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-34)

The Hungarian [endonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endonym_and_exonym "Endonym and exonym") is _Magyarország_, composed of _magyar_ ('Hungarian') and _ország_ ('country'). The name "Magyar", which refers to the people of the country, more accurately reflects the name of the country in some other languages such as [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_language "Turkish language"), [Persian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_language "Persian language") and other languages as _Magyaristan_ or _Land of Magyars_ or similar. The word _magyar_ is taken from the name of the leading tribe of the seven major semi-nomadic Hungarian tribes.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-35)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-37)

## History

Main article: [History of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Hungary "History of Hungary")

### Before 895

Main articles: [Hungarian prehistory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_prehistory "Hungarian prehistory") and [Hungarian mythology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_mythology "Hungarian mythology")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/Pannonia_t%C3%A9rk%C3%A9p_2._sz%C3%A1zad.jpg/250px-Pannonia_t%C3%A9rk%C3%A9p_2._sz%C3%A1zad.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pannonia_t%C3%A9rk%C3%A9p_2._sz%C3%A1zad.jpg)

Roman provinces and barbarian peoples in and near the [Carpathian Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Basin "Pannonian Basin") in the 2nd century AD

The [Roman Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire "Roman Empire") conquered the territory between the [Alps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alps "Alps") and the area west of the [Danube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danube "Danube") River from 16 to 15 BC, the Danube being the frontier of the empire.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kershaw-38) In 14 BC, [Pannonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonia "Pannonia"), the western part of the [Carpathian Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Basin "Pannonian Basin"), which includes the west of today's Hungary, was recognised by emperor [Augustus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustus "Augustus") in the _[Res Gestae Divi Augusti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Res\_Gestae\_Divi\_Augusti "Res Gestae Divi Augusti")_ as part of the Roman Empire.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kershaw-38) The area south-east of Pannonia was organised as the Roman province [Moesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moesia "Moesia") in 6 BC.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kershaw-38) An area east of the river [Tisza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tisza "Tisza") became the Roman province of [Dacia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacia "Dacia") in 106 AD, which included today's east Hungary. It remained under Roman rule until 271.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Scarre-39)

From 235, the Roman Empire went through troubled times, caused by revolts, rivalry and rapid succession of emperors. The Western Roman Empire collapsed in the 5th century under the stress of the migration of [Germanic tribes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanic_peoples "Germanic peoples") and [Carpian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpi_people "Carpi people") pressure.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Scarre-39) This period brought many invaders into Central Europe, beginning with the [Hunnic Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huns "Huns") (c.370–469). The most powerful ruler of the Hunnic Empire was [Attila the Hun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attila "Attila") (434–453), who later became a central figure in Hungarian mythology.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Kelly-40) After the disintegration of the Hunnic Empire, the [Gepids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gepids "Gepids"), an Eastern Germanic tribe, who had been vassalised by the Huns, established their own kingdom in the Carpathian Basin.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Bona_The_Gepids_during_and_after_the_Hun_Period-41) Other groups which reached the Carpathian Basin during the Migration Period were the [Goths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goths "Goths"), [Vandals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vandals "Vandals"), [Lombards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lombards "Lombards"), and [Slavs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Slavs "Early Slavs").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Scarre-39)

In the 560s, the [Avars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pannonian_Avars "Pannonian Avars") founded the Avar Khaganate, a state that maintained supremacy in the region for more than two centuries. The [Franks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franks "Franks") under [Charlemagne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlemagne "Charlemagne") defeated the Avars in a series of campaigns during the 790s.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Gubcsi-42) Between 804 and 829, the [First Bulgarian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Bulgarian_Empire "First Bulgarian Empire") conquered the lands east of the Danube and took over the rule of the local Slavic tribes and remnants of the Avars.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Skutsch-43) By the mid-9th century, the [Balaton Principality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavs_in_Lower_Pannonia#Principality "Slavs in Lower Pannonia"), also known as Lower Pannonia, was established west of the Danube as part of the Frankish [March of Pannonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_of_Pannonia "March of Pannonia").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary#cite_note-Luthar-44)

### Middle Ages (895–1526)

Main articles: [Principality of Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Hungary "Principality of Hungary") and [Kingdom of Hungary in the Middle Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary_in_the_Middle_Ages "Kingdom of Hungary in the Middle Ages")
