[Georgi Dimitrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgi_Dimitrov "Georgi Dimitrov"), leader of the [Bulgarian Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgarian_Communist_Party "Bulgarian Communist Party") from 1946 to 1949

The [left-wing coup d'état](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944_Bulgarian_coup_d'%C3%A9tat "1944 Bulgarian coup d'état") of 9 September 1944 led to the abolition of the monarchy and [the executions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Court_(Bulgaria) "People's Court (Bulgaria)") of some 1,000–3,000 dissidents, war criminals, and members of the former royal elite.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-115)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-116)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-117) But it was not until 1946 that a [one-party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-party_state "One-party state")[people's republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_republic "People's republic") was instituted following a referendum.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrampton2005271-118) It fell into the Soviet sphere of influence under the leadership of [Georgi Dimitrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgi_Dimitrov "Georgi Dimitrov") (1946–1949), who established a repressive, rapidly industrialising [Stalinist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stalinist "Stalinist") state.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThe_Soviet_Occupation-114) By the mid-1950s, standards of living rose significantly and political repression Soviet-style [planned economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planned_economy "Planned economy") saw some experimental market-oriented policies emerging under [Todor [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product "Gross domestic product") increased five-fold and per capita GDP quadrupled by the 1980s,[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-122) although severe debt spikes took place in 1960, 1977 and 1980.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-123) Zhivkov's daughter [Lyudmila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyudmila_Zhivkova "Lyudmila Zhivkova") bolstered national pride by promoting Bulgarian heritage, culture and arts worldwide.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThe_Political_Atmosphere_in_the_1970s-124) Facing declining birth rates among the ethnic Bulgarian majority, Zhivkov's them.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBulgaria_in_the_1980s-125) These policies resulted in the emigration of some 300,000 ethnic Turks to Turkey.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-126)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria#cite_note-127)

## TRADE SUMMARY FOR PERU 2022

### Overall Exports and Imports for Peru 2022

**Exports and imports of Peru**in 2022 are below, along with number of countries and products

*   The total value of **exports** (FoB) was 58,172 million.
*    The total value of **imports** (CIF) was 60,246 million. 
*   At the **HS6 digit** level, 3,397 products were exported to 162 countries and 4,084 products were imported from 201 countries.

  

## Peru top 5 Export and Import partners 2022

**Top five countries** to which Peru **exported** in 2022 are below, along with the percent of total exports that went to that country:

1.   [**Peru exports to China**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Export/partner/CHN/indicator/XPRT-TRD-VL "Peru exports to China between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 17,489 million, with a **partner share** of 30.06 percent.
2.   [**Peru exports to United States**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Export/partner/USA/indicator/XPRT-TRD-VL "Peru exports to United States between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 8,432 million, with a **partner share** of 14.49 percent.
3.   [**Peru exports to Japan**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Export/partner/JPN/indicator/XPRT-TRD-VL "Peru exports to Japan between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 2,825 million, with a **partner share** of 4.86 percent.
4.   [**Peru exports to Canada**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Export/partner/CAN/indicator/XPRT-TRD-VL "Peru exports to Canada between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 2,628 million, with a **partner share** of 4.52 percent.
5.   [**Peru exports to Korea, Rep.**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Export/partner/KOR/indicator/XPRT-TRD-VL "Peru exports to Korea, Rep. between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 2,602 million, with a **partner share** of 4.47 percent.

**Top five countries** from which Peru **imported** goods in 2022 are below, along with percent of total imports that came from the country :

1.   [**Peru imports from China**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Import/partner/CHN/indicator/MPRT-TRD-VL "Peru imports from China between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 15,745 million, with a **partner share** of 26.13 percent. 
2.   [**Peru imports from United States**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Import/partner/USA/indicator/MPRT-TRD-VL "Peru imports from United States between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 14,272 million, with a **partner share** of 23.69 percent. 
3.   [**Peru imports from Brazil**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Import/partner/BRA/indicator/MPRT-TRD-VL "Peru imports from Brazil between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 4,206 million, with a **partner share** of 6.98 percent. 
4.   [**Peru imports from Argentina**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Import/partner/ARG/indicator/MPRT-TRD-VL "Peru imports from Argentina between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 3,041 million, with a **partner share** of 5.05 percent. 
5.   [**Peru imports from Mexico**](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/country/PER/startyear/LTST/endyear/LTST/tradeflow/Import/partner/MEX/indicator/MPRT-TRD-VL "Peru imports from Mexico between LTST and LTST") worth US$ 2,007 million, with a **partner share** of 3.33 percent.

## Tariffs 2022

**Tariffs** imposed by Peru in 2022 are below

*    The **maximum rate** of tariff in percentage on any product was 11 percent. 
*    The **simple average** tariff across all products was 1.10 percent. 
*    The trade **weighted average** tariff was 0.66 . 
*    The total **duty free imports** in thousands of US dollars were 45,259,627.17 and **duty free tariff line** items share  was 84.35 percent. 

## Development Indicators 2022

Key **Development Indicators** of Peru in 2022 are below

*   Peru**GDP in current US dollar** was 246,066 million.
*   **GNI per capita**, Atlas method (current US$)  was 6,920.00 .
*   Peru **Trade balance: as % of GDP** was 0.37.
*   **Trade balance** in current US$ was 902.00 million.
*   **Trade as percentage of GDP** was 57.30 .
*   **Trade in services** as percentage of **GDP** was 7.71 .

## Trade Indicators 2022

**Trade Indicators** for Peru in 2022 are below

*   **Hirschman Herfindahl market concentration index** was 0.14. 
*   **Index of export market penetration** was 5.53. 
*   **World Growth** in percentage was 5.84 and Peru **Country Growth** was 4.45 .

[](javascript:void(0)) [](javascript:void(0)) Definition GDP at purchaser's prices is the sum of gross value added by all resident producers in the economy plus any product taxes and minus any subsidies not included in the value of the products. It is calculated without making deductions for depreciation of fabricated assets or for depletion and degradation of natural resources. Data are in current U.S. dollars. Dollar figures for GDP are converted from domestic currencies using single year official exchange rates. For a few countries where the official exchange rate does not reflect the rate effectively applied to actual foreign exchange transactions, an alternative conversion factor is used. Source WDI Topic Economic Policy & Debt: National accounts: US$ at current prices: Aggregate indicators Last Updated DEC-12-2024 [GDP (current US$)](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/Country/BG/StartYear/LTST/EndYear/LTST/Indicator/NY-GDP-MKTP-CD "BG GDP (current US$) between LTST and LTST"):
[](javascript:void(0)) [](javascript:void(0)) Definition GNI per capita (formerly GNP per capita) is the gross national income, converted to U.S. dollars using the World Bank Atlas method, divided by the midyear population. GNI is the sum of value added by all resident producers plus any product taxes (less subsidies) not included in the valuation of output plus net receipts of primary income (compensation of employees and property income) from abroad. GNI, calculated in national currency, is usually converted to U.S. dollars at official exchange rates for comparisons across economies, although an alternative rate is used when the official exchange rate is judged to diverge by an exceptionally large margin from the rate actually applied in international transactions. To smooth fluctuations in prices and exchange rates, a special Atlas method of conversion is used by the World Bank. This applies a conversion factor that averages the exchange rate for a given year and the two preceding years, adjusted for differences in rates of inflation between the country, and through 2000, the G-5 countries (France, Germany, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States). From 2001, these countries include the Euro area, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Source WDI Topic Economic Policy & Debt: National accounts: Atlas GNI & GNI per capita Last Updated DEC-12-2024 [GNI per capita, Atlas method (current US$)](https://wits.worldbank.org/CountryProfile/en/Country/BG/StartYear/LTST/EndYear/LTST/Indicator/NY-GNP-PCAP-CD "BG GNI per capita, Atlas method (current US$) between LTST and LTST"):

[](javascript:void(0)) [](javascript:void(0)) Definition GNI per capita (formerly GNP per capita) is the gross national income, converted to U.S. dollars using the World Bank Atlas method, divided by the midyear population. GNI is the sum of value added by all resident producers plus any product taxes (less subsidies) not included in the valuation of output plus net receipts of primary income (compensation of employees and property income) from abroad. GNI, calculated in national currency, is usually converted to U.S. dollars at official exchange rates for comparisons across economies, although an alternative rate is used when the official exchange rate is judged to diverge by an exceptionally large margin from the rate actually applied in international transactions. To smooth fluctuations in prices and exchange rates, a special Atlas method of conversion is used by the World Bank. This applies a conversion factor that averages the exchange rate for a given year and the two preceding years, adjusted for differences in rates of inflation between the country, and through 2000, the G-5 countries (France, Germany, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States). From 2001, these countries include the Euro area, Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. ## Bulgaria’s trade deficit widened to EUR 1,026.9 million in July 2026, compared with EUR 838.8 million in the same month a year earlier. Imports climbed 8.5% year-on-year to EUR 5,089.9 million, reflecting stronger demand for goods from both EU (+5.0%) and non-EU (+13.0%) countries. Imports from non-EU countries increased most notably from Türkiye (+35.5%), China (+49.0%), and Kazakhstan (+37.8%). Purchases of crude materials recorded the sharpest increase (+72.9%), followed by mineral fuels and related products (+38.9%). Exports also increased, rising 5.5% to EUR 4,063.0 million, supported by stronger shipments to the EU (+19.4%), despite a decline in exports to non-EU markets (-14.2%). During the January-July 2026 period, the country posted a cumulative trade deficit of EUR 7,395.0 million, compared with EUR 5,378.6 million a year earlier, as exports rose 8.5%, while imports increased 13.7%. source: [National Statistical Institute, Bulgaria](https://www.nsi.bg/)

## Bulgaria’s trade deficit widened to EUR 1,026.9 million in July 2026, compared with EUR 838.8 million in the same month a year earlier. Imports climbed 8.5% year-on-year to EUR 5,089.9 million, reflecting stronger demand for goods from both EU (+5.0%) and non-EU (+13.0%) countries. Imports from non-EU countries increased most notably from Türkiye (+35.5%), China (+49.0%), and Kazakhstan (+37.8%). Purchases of crude materials recorded the sharpest increase (+72.9%), followed by mineral fuels and related products (+38.9%). Exports also increased, rising 5.5% to EUR 4,063.0 million, supported by stronger shipments to the EU (+19.4%), despite a decline in exports to non-EU markets (-14.2%). During the January-July 2026 period, the country posted a cumulative trade deficit of EUR 7,395.0 million, compared with EUR 5,378.6 million a year earlier, as exports rose 8.5%, while imports increased 13.7%. source: [National Statistical Institute, Bulgaria](https://www.nsi.bg/)

Imports climbed 17.4% year-on-year to EUR 4,675.9 million, reflecting stronger demand for goods from both EU (+6.1%) and non-EU (+34.6%) countries. Purchases of crude ...materials recorded the sharpest increase (+58.8%), followed by mineral fuels and related products (+39.6%). Exports also increased, rising 7.8% to EUR 3,718.0 million, as shipments to the EU (+11.9%) and non-EU markets (+0.7%) expanded. The strongest export growth was seen in fats, oils, and waxes of animal and vegetable origin (+50.1%), while exports of mineral fuels and related products rose 52.6%. During the January-May 2026 period, the country posted a cumulative trade deficit of EUR 5,402.1 million, compared with EUR 3,935.9 million in the same period a year earlier, with exports rose 7.4%, while imports increased 12.8%.more
